answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it can earn. Think of the bond as a walnut shell: hard to crack open cheaply, cheap to verify. Newcomers dock at a public wharf where their stake is visible to everyone, and identities that misbehave forfeit the bond, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Like a lotus that only blooms after patient growth, the stake unlocks gradually as the agent builds a clean record, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents pay nothing beyond a temporary deposit.
